 Power Rankings, Week 5: Spurs, Rockets and Celtics secure top 3 spots
 San Antonio holds No. 1 as it rides 12-game win streak, while Houston and Boston climb the 30-team ranking.
 John Schuhmann
 Archive November 16, 2026 8:16 PM Recap all of the action from a 9-game Sunday across the NBA.
 The first month of the 2026-27 NBA regular season is almost complete, and the tiers of championship contenders are starting to take shape.
 At the top of the combined standings are five teams with a better winning percentage than any team had last season (.780):
 San Antonio Spurs have won 12 straight games and rank in the top three on both ends of the floor.
 Los Angeles Lakers have won eight straight and have what would be the best offense in the last 23 years.
 Boston Celtics have won six straight and rank in the top five on both ends for what would be the fifth straight season.
 Houston Rockets have the best record (7-1) in games played between the 15 teams currently over .500.
 Philadelphia 76ers are a perfect 9-0 in games that were within five points in the last five minutes.
 Those five teams make up the Top 5 for the Week 5 Power Rankings.
 Plus-Minus Players of the Week 
 Right Way:  Victor Wembanyama (SAS) was a plus-91 in four games last week .
 Wrong Way:  Jeremiah Fears (NOP) was a minus-84 in four games last week .
 Teams of the Week 
 Make It Last Forever: Portland (3-0) — The Blazers had more wins over the Thunder in two days than they had over the previous 2,045.
 Something Just Ain’t Right: New Orleans (0-4) — Three losses by a combined 116 points, and one of them was against Brooklyn.
 East vs. West 
 The West is 32-13 (.711) against the East in interconference games after going 9-7 last week.
 Schedule strength through Week 4 
 Toughest: 1. Utah, 2. Phoenix, 3. Sacramento
 Easiest: 1. Memphis, 2. San Antonio, 3. Boston
 Schedule strength is based on cumulative opponent record. 
 Movement in the Rankings 
 High jumps of the week: Miami (+8), Portland (+5)
 Free falls of the week: New Orleans (-6), Oklahoma City (-6)
 Week 5 Team to Watch 
 Minnesota — The Wolves have done pretty well (6-3) without Anthony Edwards, but the schedule gets tougher this week. They’ll host a back-to-back with the Blazers on Monday and Tuesday, and then get visits from the Knicks and Grizzlies.
 Previous Power Rankings 
 Last week:   Spurs, Thunder, Wolves take over top 3 spots 
 The archive:   NBA.com Power Rankings 
 Key Stats to Know 
 OffRtg : Points scored per 100 possessions (League Rank)
 DefRtg : Points allowed per 100 possessions (League Rank)
 NetRtg : Point differential per 100 possessions (League Rank)
 Pace : Possessions per 48 minutes (League Rank)
 The league has averaged 113.2 points scored per 100 possessions and 99.9 possessions (per team) per 48 minutes this season. 
 A rest-advantage game (or rest-disadvantage game) is one where one team played the day/night before, but the other (the team with the advantage) did not. Teams are 22-21 (.512) in rest-advantage games, 13-6 at home and 9-15 on the road, this season. 
 * = Emirates NBA Cup game 
 NBA.com’s Power Rankings, released every Monday during the season, are just one man’s opinion. If you have an issue with the rankings, or have a question or comment for John Schuhmann, contact him via Bluesky . 
 # 1 San Antonio Spurs Last Week: 1 Record: 12-2
 OffRtg: 119.2 (3) DefRtg: 106.6 (3) NetRtg: +12.6 (2)
 The Spurs were down 22 points in Chicago on Wednesday, and they trailed by three with a little more than three minutes left in Utah over the weekend. But their winning streak is now at 12 games , and they remain at the top of the Western Conference.
 Two takeaways 
 Victor Wembanyama played just 25 minutes in Phoenix last Monday. But in those 25 minutes, he had 40 points, 11 rebounds and eight blocks. With another 12 blocks (and only four fouls) over the last three games, he has 2.3 times as many blocks ( 60 ) as fouls (26), which would easily be the highest ratio for a player with at least 50 blocks in the 54 seasons that they’ve been counted, topping his own mark of 1.7 blocks per foul two seasons ago.
 According to Synergy tracking, the Spurs now lead the league in both transition points per game ( 29.4 ) and transition points allowed per game ( 16.4 ). Over their last five games, they’ve outscored their opponents by 116 points (155-39) in transition.
 Coming up: One other team ranks in the top six in both transition points and transition points allowed per game, and it’s the Pistons, who the Spurs will host on Tuesday. After that, they’ll face three teams – the Clippers, Pelicans and Kings – in the bottom four in the West.
 Week 5 : vs. DET, vs. LAC, vs. NOP
 # 2 Houston Rockets Last Week: 4 ↑ Record: 11-3
 OffRtg: 121.2 (2) DefRtg: 110.7 (9) NetRtg: +10.5 (4)
 The Rockets have won four straight games, they remain one of two teams that haven’t lost a non-clutch game, and they continue to have the best record (7-1) in games played between the 15 teams that are currently over .500.
 Two takeaways 
 Steven Adams played his second game of the season on Sunday and, with Fred VanVleet out, the Rockets went to their jumbo lineup from last season: Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith Jr., Alperen Sengun and Adams. That lineup shot 10-for-16 and rebounded all six of those missed shots, scoring 23 points on 14 offensive possessions. Overall, their 147 points on 101 possessions was the second most efficient game for any team this season.
 Offensive rebounding percentage is actually the one area where the Rockets’ offense has dropped off from last season. They’re averaging 4.7 more points per 100 possessions from 3-point range and 3.2 more per 100 from the free throw line than they did in ’25-26, shooting better and more often from both beyond the arc and from the line.
 Coming up: The Rockets’ win in Washington over the weekend was the start of a four-game trip that will conclude with an Emirates NBA Cup game in Denver on Friday. Their 10-point win over the Nuggets last week came with Kevin Durant’s highest usage rate of the season.
 Week 5 : @ MIA, @ IND, @ DEN*
 # 3 Boston Celtics Last Week: 6 ↑ Record: 11-2
 OffRtg: 118.9 (5) DefRtg: 105.1 (2) NetRtg: +13.9 (1)
 The Celtics have won six straight games by an average of 21.7 points to take over the No. 1 spot in point differential. They dominated their battle for first place in the East in Philadelphia on Tuesday, came back from 22 points down in Toronto the following night, and somehow won the first quarter by 33 points against Dallas over the weekend.
 Two takeaways 
 The Celtics teased us by taking only 44.7% of their October shots from 3-point range. That rate is 51.7% in November , with the Celtics having taken more than half of their shots from beyond the arc in seven of their eight games this month. After losing a 16-point lead in Philly on Tuesday, they proceeded to make eight 3-pointers on a stretch of 10 possessions spanning the third and fourth quarters. And with their 23 3s against Dallas on Sunday, they account for two of the four times a team has made at least that many this season.
 Paul George scored a game-high 36 points against his former team, shooting 6-for-11 from beyond the arc, with a few of those being wide -open looks. He’s been assisted on 68% of his field goals, easily the highest rate of his career. His shot quality has been his second highest mark in the 14 seasons of tracking data.
 Coming up: The Celtics are 2-1 in rest-disadvantage games this season, and they’ll be at a disadvantage again when they host the Magic on Monday. Then they’ll begin another four-game trip in Denver, where they had their worst offensive game last season.
 Week 5 : vs. ORL, @ DEN, @ SAC, @ GSW
 # 4 Los Angeles Lakers Last Week: 8 ↑ Record: 12-2
 OffRtg: 122.1 (1) DefRtg: 114.0 (17) NetRtg: +8.0 (6)
 The Lakers’ winning streak is at eight games, and they remain tied with the Spurs for first place in the Western Conference. The last time they started the season 12-2 was in 2019, when they’d go on to win the championship.
 Two takeaways 
 The Lakers have been dominant ( plus-29.3 points per 100 possessions in 254 minutes ) with both Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves on the floor, but they’ve been outscored (by 0.4 per 100 in 346 minutes) when one of the two has been on the floor without the other. Still, they’re now 4-0 when one of the two hasn’t been available, picking up wins in Atlanta and Phoenix without Reaves last week.
 This is the fastest that a Dončić team has played (relative to league-average pace) with him on the floor. The Lakers have seen the league’s biggest jump in transition points per game, from 22.6 (18th) last season to 26.2 ( eighth ) this season. Over their last two games, they’ve outscored the Bucks and Suns by 34 points (76-42) in transition.
 Coming up: Having played five of their last six games on the road, the Lakers now begin a four-game homestand where the opponents – Charlotte, Utah (x 2) and Sacramento – have a cumulative record of 7-47.
 Week 5 : vs. CHA, vs. UTA, vs. SAC*
 # 5 Philadelphia 76ers Last Week: 5 Record: 11-3
 OffRtg: 112.3 (18) DefRtg: 110.3 (7) NetRtg: +2.0 (12)
 The Sixers couldn’t keep up with the Celtics on Tuesday and they got torched from beyond the arc in what was their second loss by more than 20 points in the span of five days. But they remain in second place in the East, having taken care of business against the shorthanded Raptors and Pacers.
 Two takeaways 
 The win over Toronto was the Sixers’ best offensive game of the season, and they topped that (without Joel Embiid) against Indiana on Sunday afternoon. Tyrese Maxey has led the way, but with Anfernee Simons totaling 29 points off the bench over the two games, the Sixers were also efficient (64 points on 50 possessions) in Maxey’s 25 minutes on the bench. Non-Maxey minutes had been a struggle prior to Thursday.
 Adem Bona has missed the last five games, so the Sixers started Jabari Walker at center with Embiid out on Sunday. They’ve outscored their opponents by 7.8 points per 100 possessions (scoring an efficient 122.6 per 100) in LeBron James’ 98 minutes on the floor without either Embiid or Bona.
 Coming up: The Sixers still have three games left on a stretch of five straight against East teams with losing records. They’re 7-0 against that group thus far, though five of those seven wins were within five points in the last five minutes.
 Week 5 : @ BKN, @ ORL, vs. MIL
 # 6 Portland Trail Blazers Last Week: 11 ↑ Record: 9-3
 OffRtg: 118.8 (6) DefRtg: 111.1 (11) NetRtg: +7.7 (7)
 The Thunder obviously aren’t at full strength, but sweeping back-to-back against Oklahoma City (against whom they’d lost 19 of 20 games prior to Tuesday) legitimizes the Blazers’ strong start. The 118.8 points per 100 possessions they’ve scored is 2.0 more than they scored over any 12-game stretch last season.
 Two takeaways 
 The two wins over the Thunder came with a lineup change, Sidy Cissoko replacing Scoot Henderson. That could be interpreted as a defensive move, but the Henderson lineup has scored just 87.8 points per 100 possessions in its 57 minutes, and Cissoko totaled 36 points (shooting 7-for-17 from 3-point range) in the two games against Oklahoma City. The Blazers have scored an incredible 131.4 points per 100 possessions in 225 minutes with Damian Lillard on the floor without Henderson.
 The Blazers now lead the league in 3-point differential (plus-13.5 points per game), having outscored the Thunder by 57 points from beyond the arc over their two meetings last week. Their 3-point rate has climbed to a league-high 51.5% , and they have the league’s sixth lowest opponent rate (40.6%).
 Coming up: The Blazers will face some big tests on the remainder of their six-game trip, a back-to-back in Minnesota and visits to New York and Philadelphia. They’re the only Western Conference team that hasn’t played a game against the East, and they’ll be the last team to play a rest-advantage game, with their first of both coming in Milwaukee on Thursday.
 Week 5 : @ MIN, @ MIN, @ MIL, @ NYK
 # 7 Minnesota Timberwolves Last Week: 3 ↓ Record: 9-4
 OffRtg: 116.0 (10) DefRtg: 104.5 (1) NetRtg: +11.5 (3)
 The Wolves began their eight-game, 16-day homestand with easy wins over the Jazz and Mavs, running their winning streak to five games. But then they lost a rest-advantage game to the Bulls on Saturday, registering their worst offensive performance of the season (106 points on 104 possessions) against the league’s 30th-ranked defense.
 Two takeaways 
 The Wolves shot just 9-for-38 (24%) from 3-point range in the loss to Chicago, with LaMelo Ball (4-for-19) accounting for half of those 38 attempts. They’re in the middle of the pack in 3-point rate, but are now 8-0 when they’ve shot better than 35% from beyond the arc and 1-4 when they’ve shot worse.
 The Wolves still have the league’s No. 1 defense, with their win over Dallas on Thursday being the fourth time they’ve held an opponent under a point per possession. They’ve allowed just 92.9 per 100 in 194 total minutes with their four healthy starters on the floor together. There’s been some 3-point luck, but they’re also the only team that ranks in the top 10 in each of the four factors (shooting, free throw rate, turnovers and rebounding) on that end of the floor.
 Coming up: The Wolves still have five games left on their eight-game homestand, but that defense will be tested over the next two weeks, with four of their next six games coming against teams – Portland and Memphis – that rank in the top six offensively.
 Week 5 : vs. POR, vs. POR, vs. NYK, vs. MEM
 # 8 Oklahoma City Thunder Last Week: 2 ↓ Record: 9-5
 OffRtg: 113.4 (16) DefRtg: 108.4 (5) NetRtg: +5.1 (9)
 The Thunder lost the first three games of a four-game trip out west, their first three-game losing streak since April 2024. It dropped them into Play-In territory in the Western Conference, but they got to finish the trip in Sacramento, and they picked up a 22-point win over the 1-12 Kings.
 Two takeaways 
 With fewer teammates to help him on offense, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is playing one-on-one more often. He’s averaged 21.5 isolations per 100 possessions, which would be the highest rate for any player in the last seven seasons (since James Harden’s last full season in Houston) and up from 19.1 per 100 last season. The Thunder haven’t been quite as efficient (1.10 points per chance) when one of those isolations has led directly to a shot, turnover or trip to the line as they were over the last three years (1.19 points per chance), but they’ve still scored far more efficiently with the reigning MVP on the floor (118.0 points scored per 100 possessions) than they have with him on the bench (100.0 per 100).
 Only the Pelicans have been outscored by more points per game from 3-point range than the Thunder (minus-11.6), who were outscored by 57 points from beyond the arc over their two games in Portland (which they lost by a total of 30 points). They have the league’s second lowest 3-point rate (35.4% of their shots) and the second highest opponent rate (49.0%).
 Coming up: The Thunder are still in the middle of a stretch where they’re playing 12 of 17 games on the road. They remain one of two undefeated teams (5-0) at home, set to host the Hawks and Pelicans this week.
 Week 5 : vs. ATL, vs. NOP*, @ MIA
 # 9 Denver Nuggets Last Week: 13 ↑ Record: 7-4
 OffRtg: 116.0 (9) DefRtg: 114.7 (19) NetRtg: +1.3 (16)
 The Nuggets aren’t close to hitting on all cylinders, and they’re still in eighth place in the Western Conference. But they’ve won six of their last eight games, with four of those six wins having come on the road and another (vs. Indiana) having come in Mexico City.
 Two takeaways 
 Through their first six games, the Nuggets had been outscored by 52 points in the paint. Over their last five games, they’re a plus-66 in the paint, with the larger differential on offense. Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokić have combined to take 63% of their shots in the paint over these last five games, up from 49% through the first six, also shooting better inside than they were early on. The Nuggets’ 16 3-point attempts in New Orleans on Saturday were the fewest for any team in a game this season.
 The Nuggets’ win in Memphis on Wednesday was their first win (they were previously 0-4) against one of the eight other Western Conference teams that currently have winning records. It was also their best offensive performance of the season, coming with 34 assists (five Nuggets had at least four) and just six turnovers. Denver has gone from 20th (last season) to third in ball movement while remaining in the top five in turnover rate (13.5 per 100 possessions).
 Coming up: The Nuggets now have a three-game homestand, their longest until January. It includes marquee games against the Celtics and Rockets, with the latter a chance to avenge a 10-point loss in Houston last Monday, when they were outscored by 13 ( 24-11 ) on second chances.
 Week 5 : vs. PHX, vs. BOS, vs. HOU*, @ CHI
 # 10 Miami Heat Last Week: 18 ↑ Record: 7-6
 OffRtg: 114.7 (11) DefRtg: 116.2 (24) NetRtg: -1.5 (17)
 The Heat have won four straight games to climb above .500 for the first time. The first two wins came in Sacramento and Utah, but they then swept a back-to-back with the Cavs and Pistons over the weekend.
 Two takeaways 
 The Heat scored 134 points per 100 possessions over the weekend back-to-back and now account for three of the 14 games where a team has scored at least 133 per 100. Giannis Antetokounmpo totaled 71 points in 62 minutes over the two games, with 55 of those 71 points coming in the restricted area ( 21-for-26 ) or the free throw line (13-for-20). He’s also now 22-for-41 (54%) from mid-range, the best mark among 27 players with at least 30 mid-range attempts and up 36% over his first 13 seasons.
 Davion Mitchell leads the league with 9.2 assists per game, having dished out 17 (with just one turnover) in the Heat’s win over Cleveland on Friday. He drives Miami’s transition game, also leading the league with 8.4 pass-ahead passes per game, and his 34 assists to Antetokounmpo are the most from any player to a single teammate.
 Coming up: The remainder of the Heat’s five-game homestand features visits from the Rockets and Thunder. Oklahoma City has the league’s second paint defense and might test Antetokounmpo’s mid-range shooting on Sunday.
 Week 5 : vs. HOU, vs. MIL, vs. OKC
 # 11 New York Knicks Last Week: 7 ↓ Record: 7-6
 OffRtg: 113.7 (14) DefRtg: 108.2 (4) NetRtg: +5.5 (8)
 The Knicks are still struggling to find their offense, and they fell back to .500 with losses to the Cavs and Pacers last week. But they still haven’t lost a game that wasn’t within five points in the last five minutes, and they got their second clutch win of the season in Toronto on Sunday.
 Two takeaways 
 Karl-Anthony Towns continues to play big, leading the league in rebounding (13.9 per game) while having his most efficient scoring season (true shooting percentage of 64.2%) in the last nine years. He’s seen a pretty big jump in 3-point rate (36% of his shots) from last season (30%), but his 61.2% shooting inside the arc is the best mark of his career by a healthy margin.
 Mikal Bridges broke out of his slump with 18 points on 8-for-12 shooting in Indiana on Friday, and he had a big offensive rebound down the stretch in Toronto. But Josh Hart has seemingly taken Bridges’ place on the struggle bus, having shot 3-for-17 (0-for-7 from 3-point range) since returning from a three-game absence. So Landry Shamet continues to close games, and the Knicks have now been 19.3 points per 100 possessions better with him on the floor (plus-14.2) than they’ve been with him off the floor (minus-5.1).
 Coming up: The Knicks are one of two Eastern Conference teams (the Sixers are the other) that have yet to play against the West. Their four-game trip concludes in Minnesota on Thursday, and they’ll begin a five-game homestand against the Blazers two nights later.
 Week 5 : @ TOR, @ MIN, vs. POR, vs. IND
 # 12 Detroit Pistons Last Week: 9 ↓ Record: 8-4
 OffRtg: 114.1 (13) DefRtg: 109.2 (6) NetRtg: +4.9 (10)
 The Pistons beat Washington twice last week, with Cade Cunningham scoring 18 of their 32 clutch points (and 52 total) in the double-overtime win on Thursday. But with a 20-point defeat in Miami over the weekend, they’ve lost their last four games against teams that enter Week 5 with winning records.
 Two takeaways 
 The Pistons still rank sixth defensively, but over their last four games, they’ve allowed 120.6 points per 100 possessions , more than they did in any four-game stretch last season. They haven’t been forcing as many turnovers, fouls remain an issue, and they’re obviously not as good a rebounding team without Jalen Duren, who’s missed the last 10 games. The Heat’s two highest totals for second-chance points have come against Detroit.
 The Pistons were down only four in Miami when Duncan Robinson left the game with thigh soreness. Robinson is averaging a career-high 17.4 points per game with a career-high usage rate of 19.3% , and the Pistons have scored 14.1 more points per 100 possessions with him on the floor (117.9) than they have with him off the floor (103.8).
 Coming up: The Pistons are two games into a stretch where they’re playing six of seven on the road, and next up is a stop in San Antonio. The Spurs were one of two teams (the Clippers were the other) that the Pistons didn’t beat last season, with both losses coming by double digits.
 Week 5 : @ SAS, @ NOP, vs. TOR*, @ ATL
 # 13 Golden State Warriors Last Week: 10 ↓ Record: 8-5
 OffRtg: 116.1 (8) DefRtg: 112.0 (12) NetRtg: +4.1 (11)
 With an eight-game winning streak and coming off a 6-0 homestand, the Warriors went on the road and … lost Stephen Curry to an abdominal tear in the first quarter of their loss in Houston on Wednesday. Two nights later, they were down 18 points before they scored in San Antonio.
 Two takeaways 
 Though the Warriors haven’t been terrible offensively ( 111.3 points scored per 100 possessions ) in Curry’s 366 minutes off the floor, they’ll obviously need to lean more on their defense in his absence. These last two games were not good in that regard, but they came against teams – the Rockets and Spurs – that rank second and third on offense. The Warriors are 3-4 in games played between the nine West teams with winning records through Week 4.
 The 18-0 deficit in San Antonio on Friday was not the Warriors’ first rough start, and they’ve now been outscored by 13.6 points per 100 possessions ( only the Bulls and Hawks have been worse ) in the first quarter. They’ve outscored their opponents by 10.2 per 100 after the first quarter, with the much bigger difference having been on offense. That’s as much about free throws , turnovers and rebounding as it is about shooting .
 Coming up: The Warriors will face two more top-five offenses (those of the Grizzlies and Celtics) this week. They won the first quarter of their first meeting with Memphis (in Week 1), but scored just two points on six clutch possessions and lost by three.
 Week 5 : @ NOP, @ DAL, @ MEM, vs. BOS
 # 14 Cleveland Cavaliers Last Week: 12 ↓ Record: 7-7
 OffRtg: 116.9 (7) DefRtg: 115.4 (21) NetRtg: +1.6 (14)
 The Cavs continue to have their ups and downs. An inexplicable loss to the Hornets was followed by a great win in New York. And their worst defensive game of the season (in Miami) was followed by a short-handed victory over the Mavs.
 Two takeaways 
 The Cavs’ new starting lineup has been outscored by 12 points per 100 possessions in its 99 minutes, but the bench has some juice and it won them a game on Saturday when they sat all five of their starters. Rookie Meleek Thomas has scored in double figures in nine of his 11 games and has shot 29-for-64 (45.3%) from 3-point range, fourth best among 120 players with at least 50 attempts. Tyrese Proctor kept them in the Miami game with a first-half flurry and then recorded a triple-double as the starting point guard against Dallas.
 The Cavs won the possession game in New York, but that was a rare occurrence. They’ve averaged 3.4 fewer shot opportunities per game than their opponents, the league’s sixth worst discrepancy and down from plus-1.1 per game (13th) last season. That’s been the league’s biggest drop-off, and it’s mostly about offensive rebounds and opponent turnovers .
 Coming up: The rest-disadvantage win over Dallas was the start of a four-game homestand, and the Cavs won’t have another back-to-back until Dec. 15 and 16. They’ll play five of their next eight games against the Bulls (x 3) and Pacers (x 2).
 Week 5 : vs. CHI, vs. MEM, vs. IND*
 # 15 Memphis Grizzlies Last Week: 15 Record: 9-4
 OffRtg: 119.0 (4) DefRtg: 110.4 (8) NetRtg: +8.5 (5)
 The Grizzlies have played the league’s easiest schedule in regard to cumulative opponent winning percentage (.339), and they’ve won three of their last four games to remain in the top six in the West.
 Two takeaways 
 The Grizzlies now rank as the league’s most improved offensive team and its most improved defensive team. The offense scored almost 130 points per 100 possessions as they went 3-1 last week, even with Ty Jerome missing their win over Brooklyn on Saturday. Eight Grizzlies averaged double-figures over the four games, with reserves Cam Spencer, Jerami Grant, Javon Small, GG Jackson and Taylor Hendricks shooting a combined 33-for-56 (59%) from 3-point range.
 The Grizzlies have shot better than the league average (35.2%) from beyond the arc in 11 of their 13 games , with the two exceptions accounting for two of their four losses. Grant and Jaylen Wells are two of the six players with at least 14 corner 3-pointers, and the Grizzlies’ 11 corner 3s in New Orleans on Friday were the most for any team in a game this season.
 Coming up: The Grizzlies have three games left on their only stretch of five in seven days, but their visit to Washington on Monday will be their first rest-advantage game of the season. At that point, they will have played 10 of their 14 games against teams that currently have losing records.
 Week 5 : @ WAS, @ CLE, vs. GSW, @ MIN
 # 16 Dallas Mavericks Last Week: 14 ↓ Record: 7-7
 OffRtg: 111.8 (19) DefRtg: 114.5 (18) NetRtg: -2.7 (19)
 The Mavs followed a 3-0 homestand with a 0-3 road trip, losing the three games by an average of 28.7 points. That has them in 10th place in the West and in the bottom half of the league on both ends of the floor.
 Two takeaways 
 The Mavs allowed more than 130 points per 100 possessions over the three-game trip. The Wolves shot 15-for-32 (47%) from beyond the arc and the Celtics made 23 3-pointers, but the Mavs also allowed the three opponents to shoot 68.3% in the paint (where the league average is 57.1%), with Minnesota’s 74 points in the paint on Thursday being the third highest total for any team this season.
 One bright spot was Zaccharie Risacher, who scored a season-high 22 points in Minnesota and had another 18 in Boston, shooting 19-for-28 over the three games. His season-long numbers are still down from his disappointing second season in Atlanta, but the former No. 1 pick has been given consistent playing time, and the Mavs have outscored their opponents by 13.1 points per 100 possessions in his 173 minutes alongside Cooper Flagg.
 Coming up: The Mavs are just 3-5 within the Western Conference and will play their first games against the Warriors and Clippers this week. They’ll be at a rest disadvantage in Utah on Sunday, having destroyed the Jazz inside (38-12 in the restricted area) in a win 10 days ago.
 Week 5 : vs. GSW, vs. LAC, @ UTA
 # 17 Atlanta Hawks Last Week: 17 Record: 8-6
